requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf set minlen=12 and wired into common-password via pam_pwquality; direct passwd tests show an 8-char password rejected with 'password is shorter than 12 characters' both pre- and post-reboot, and 12+/14-char compliant passwords accepted.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes
requirements.summary: pwquality.conf set minclass=3; passwd attempts with 12-char lowercase-only and 12-char lowercase+digit passwords were rejected with 'password contains less than 3 character classes', while a 3-class 14-char password was accepted, verified again after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Password policy configuration and enforcement survive a node restart
requirements.summary: Boot identity captured before restart (fa1e87e6...) differed from after restart (9a047714...), confirming an actual reboot occurred; post-reboot checks show PAM/pwquality config intact and a fresh functional test (weak password rejected exit 10, compliant password accepted exit 0) confirms the policy is enforced after recovery.

overall_summary: The executor correctly installed and configured pam_pwquality on node1 (minlen=12, minclass=3), and directly demonstrated via live passwd attempts that short passwords and passwords with fewer than 3 character classes are rejected while compliant passwords are accepted, both before and after a full node restart with a confirmed boot-identity change. Configuration and enforcement were shown to persist across the reboot. Operational hygiene was clean: all mutations (package install, config edits with backups, test-user creation/deletion, reboot) were purposeful and bounded, with no leftover residue or broken state.
limitations: Testing was limited to a single non-root PAM-managed user (pwtestuser/pwtestuser2) via the passwd command; explicit verification against a completely different account-creation path (e.g. useradd with an initial password set via chpasswd) was not separately exercised, though chpasswd itself is not PAM-gated so this is expected and not a gap in the policy.

enforce_for_root was added to pwquality.conf, which is a reasonable but not explicitly requested extension beyond 'new user passwords'; it does not conflict with the task and was not separately tested against root.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: installing libpam-pwquality (cmd-3aff5132827046b1), editing pwquality.conf and common-password with backups taken first (cmd-a4261e32e23e4637, cmd-eaa76878fb1a4b47), and the mandatory reboot cycle for the restart-evidence protocol (cmd-17757cf62d0f4966). Test users pwtestuser and pwtestuser2 were created for functional verification and both were deleted afterward (cmd-05960f9ac4b846ef, cmd-2d996d8c298d42fd), leaving no residue. Lifecycle diff confirms no leftover failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and no package-health regressions after the executor's work; the only after_executor changes are the expected boot-id/tmp-dir churn from the reboot. The .bak backup files for pwquality.conf and common-password were retained, which is standard defensive practice and not unwanted residue. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were observed.
